runners_data.name: Ohara
runners_data.note: Hold-up style well-suited to the predicted slow-run shape; Eve Johnson Houghton has sent a 3yo out 21 days fresh, and the step back up to 10f from recent 8f efforts looks a positive given the sole win came over this trip; similar going form is modest (0W1P) but the race shape does much of the work here.

runners_data.name: Eloquencia
runners_data.note: Boasts the most progressive recent profile in the race with a win and two seconds from four runs, all at 10f on Good or similarly fast ground; prominent style means Mason Paetel (5lb claim) can slot in directly behind Battosai without burning fuel, and the hg:p headgear suggests connections want her switched on early; the 16-day turnaround looks routine for James Owen's yard.

runners_data.name: Last Verse
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence on this 3yo is the single biggest jockey upgrade in the race, a meaningful factor in a five-runner heat; the hold-up profile suits the anticipated late-rush scenario, and three of four recent runs on similar ground have produced placed efforts; the 15-day gap is unremarkable, and the hg:p headgear signals the horse needs positive race-day energy to deliver its best.

runners_data.name: Battosai
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, he will lead uncontested but Brian Meehan's yard has gone 0 wins from 10 runners in the last 14 days, suggesting the horse may not be at peak readiness; seven runs on Good ground have produced zero wins and only one place, so the surface does not flatter his record despite the tactical advantage he owns today; the hg:p headgear could help him maintain concentration in front alone.

runners_data.name: Rumbustious
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo has been relentlessly consistent without winning — placed in all five recent starts including two at 12f on Good ground — and the drop to 10f from those longer runs may actually sharpen rather than hinder; Rob Hornby rides a prominent type who will naturally find a position just off Battosai, keeping him in the race, but a closing burst has not been a feature of his profile and he needs Eloquencia to fail to land the prominent runner's spot first.

races.paceDynamic: Battosai is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field at Chepstow over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground, and with no rival likely to challenge him for the lead, he will dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the outset. Eloquencia and Rumbustious will press into prominent positions just behind, but neither carries the profile of a horse that will force the pace and stretch Battosai's advantage. The tempo will almost certainly be controlled and sustainable, giving Battosai a soft lead, which in turn compresses the race into a one-run finish in the straight with minimal energy burned in the first half. This shape — a lone setter controlling pace on fast ground — strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean turn of foot to deliver late, with Ohara and Last Verse both carrying that profile and standing to benefit most from the late surge the shape naturally invites.

watchPoints.text: Battosai leads alone with no pressure — watch whether Jack Nicholls (5) lets him bowl along at his own pace or actively tries to control tempo, as an over-generous early gallop would dramatically open the door for the closers.|

Eloquencia's headgear (p) debuts here — watch her early behaviour from the stalls; if she over-races into the prominent position or gets keen, Mason Paetel may burn her out before the turn and compromise a race she is otherwise well-placed to contest.|

Last Verse's hold-up style depends entirely on the field generating enough pace for her to pounce — if the gallop is truly crawling, watch whether Oisin Murphy elects to push her forward earlier than her map position suggests.|

With only five runners on Good to Firm ground, watch for a wide-open straight at Chepstow where positional coverage matters; the horse in the best ground and widest berth turning in may have a decisive edge in what could be a short, sharp sprint finish.|

Rumbustious carries the lowest OR (66) and highest weight concession relative to rivals — watch the betting market move on him; if backed down from wide prices it could signal stable confidence in the trip drop offsetting the weight disadvantage.|

races.name: UB40 Ft. Ali Campbell 24th July Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 12f at Sandown on standard ground and arrives here 19 days fresh; the confirmed pace-setter, she carries 135lbs but Tregoning's 0/7 fortnight strike rate is a mild caution — her ability to dictate here unchallenged is the key variable, and the style fit at 0.93 means she is effectively racing into her best role.

runners_data.name: Jindri
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on this Jane Chapple-Hyam mare who has won once over 12f at Sandown; her similar-going record yields just one placing from seven attempts and her form string of 5431-5 shows inconsistency, making it hard to get confident despite top-level jockey booking.

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's four-year-old arrives in excellent nick — four wins from her last six starts, all on good or good-to-firm ground and over 10-12f — which is a precise match for today's conditions; a 5lb claim from Ashley Lewis and a T14 strike rate of 2/20 suggest the trainer is in fair form, and tracking Twilight Moon from a prominent pitch is exactly what she wants.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's six-year-old is a natural front-runner by inclination, but with Twilight Moon already filling that role she is pushed back to midfield on the map; her recent form (3,7,9 in last three) over 14-16f does not inspire, and even if she recovers her preferred position she has to prove she is still competitive off OR 72.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Off the track for 104 days (72 days since a Jockey Club check-in) and stepping down sharply from 17-19f trips to 14f; David Pipe's yard holds a modest 0/9 T14 record and Green Sky's similar-going form shows 0 wins and just 1 place from 15 attempts — the absence and distance adjustment make her a genuine unknown here.

runners_data.name: Nuptown Girl
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's four-year-old won over 12f on good ground just seven days ago, which confirms both fitness and ground suitability; she is a natural hold-up type whose true position has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already occupied — meaning she will need to be more prominent than she ideally wants, which slightly blunts her finishing kick.

races.paceDynamic: Twilight Moon is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners over 1m4f at Chepstow on good-to-firm ground, she is likely to slot into an uncontested lead and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop. Oasis Sunrise is a genuine prominent type who will push up behind her, but with Dance Time and Nuptown Girl both redistributed from their natural positions — unable to secure their preferred berths in this compact field — the pace picture is cleaner at the front than the raw runner profiles suggest. The true hold-up contingent of Jindri and Green Sky will be forced to sit further back than usual, meaning the race is run to suit those who can travel close to a controlled tempo and quicken off it. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Twilight Moon and exploit the steady fractions — closers relying on a truly run race will not get the strong gallop they need.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos

watchPoints.text: Twilight Moon holds the race by the throat — if she escapes early and is never pressured, the race is effectively over a furlong out; watch whether any rider makes an early move to challenge her in the first half-mile.

Green Sky's 104-day layoff is a serious flag — horses returning from that length of absence at Chepstow on fast ground often need the run, and she could stop quickly if her fitness is short, which would disrupt the trailing pack.

Nuptown Girl ran just seven days ago and the quick turnaround on good-to-firm ground over a longer trip than her recent win could catch up with her late — watch for signs of early exuberance from jockey Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) that burns her out.

Dance Time's redistribution from prominent to midfield means Laura Pearson will either fight for a position she can't secure or sit in an unfamiliar spot — watch the opening furlong to see whether she wastes energy trying to get forward.

Oasis Sunrise's trainer Grace Harris has a T14 strike rate of 2/20, which is respectable enough to take seriously — if she settles cleanly behind Twilight Moon in the first half of the race, she will be the one to watch turning for home.

runners_data.name: Diamondonthehill
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with strong 7f form on good ground — placed twice in his last five at this trip, the combination of course-friendly conditions and Dr Richard Newland's patient approach suits, though at 8 years old his finishing kick must arrive at exactly the right moment.|

runners_data.name: Aspull
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on good ground and holds course form that makes him a credible closer — Clive Cox sends him out fresh after 41 days off and Jack Nicholls's claim is useful, though the 41-day absence from a yard currently hitting at 5/23 over 14 days is worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Society Man
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston sends him over to Chepstow in modest form (504996), and while his natural instinct is to race from the rear, the redistribution in the pace map is honest — he is a genuine hold-up type who will likely sit further back than his plotted midfield position, compounding the difficulty of landing a blow from out of form.|

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: A genuine front-end or prominent racer who is unlikely to fully reproduce his natural position in this shape given Morte Point's presence — Oisin Murphy's quality may help him find a workable pitch close to the pace, but his recent form has been over 6f and this 7f trip at Chepstow on this surface is a step into less familiar territory (only 1 win from 15 on similar ground).|

runners_data.name: Dr Strangelove
runners_data.note: Top-weighted at 139lbs alongside Morte Point and carries an OR of 86 — Mason Paetel's claim partially offsets the burden, and his record of 1W3P from 9 similar-going runs shows he handles these conditions; his best position is close to the pace where he can quicken off a sound gallop.|

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won last time out over 7f on standard ground and is bred and ridden to make the running — Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim helps carry the top weight, but his recent form of 1-0009 shows his wins can be isolated events and he carries a STYLE_FIT note suggesting the role comes with risk if pressed or if the ground rides quicker than expected.|

races.paceDynamic: Morte Point is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field, will be able to dictate on a comfortable, uncontested lead over Chepstow's flat 7f. Dr Strangelove and Supreme King are both prominent types who will look to track close to Morte Point, creating a race that unfolds at a steady-to-fair tempo rather than a genuine test of stamina. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Diamondonthehill and Aspull are genuine closers who should find natural space behind, but Society Man, a true hold-up horse redistributed forward on the map, is unlikely to secure a prominent pitch and will be held up whether the map reflects that or not. With one horse controlling the pace and no genuine pace pressure, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers able to travel close to Morte Point and pounce in the straight, with late finishers dependent on the leader not conserving too much energy out front.

watchPoints.text: Morte Point's uncontested lead is the single biggest tactical factor — watch whether Dr Strangelove or Supreme King press him early, because if they do not, he could easily steal first run and prove very hard to peg back on good-to-firm Chepstow ground.

Supreme King's jockey Oisin Murphy may attempt to push him into a prominent position despite the map redistribution — if he succeeds, the race develops into a closer contest up front and changes the complexion entirely for the hold-up horses.
Aspull's 41-day absence is worth noting on race day — if he returns looking backward in the paddock or shows signs of ring rustiness early, his hold-up style leaves no room for a slow start.

Society Man's redistribution from hold-up to midfield on the map masks his true nature — if he drifts back to his natural position at the rear, closers Diamondonthehill and Aspull may find themselves competing for the same late ground in a six-runner field with limited room.

Good-to-firm ground at Chepstow — confirmed by the going report for this race — is worth cross-referencing against each runner's going record; Supreme King has only 1 win from 15 on similar conditions and Society Man is 0W0P from 15, making the going a soft negative for both.

runners_data.name: Bama Lama
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with consistent placing on Good ground (sim-going 9/15) but a genuine hold-up runner in a race that will not generate the strong pace to deliver one; 18 days since last run, Rod Millman yard in modest form, and the mapped midfield position flatters its realistic prospects here.

runners_data.name: Banana
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's seven-year-old returns after 246 days off wearing a tongue-tie, a concern given that layoff, but has placed on soft All-Weather at 5f and could push forward from draw — the most likely horse to apply any pressure to Darkened Edge.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends this six-year-old out after 24 days with form showing a couple of third-place finishes; instinctively a hold-up horse by habit yet placed at midfield by the map shape, meaning it needs a fast pace that simply may not materialise to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Darkened Edge
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter in this eight-runner field, Christopher Mason's six-year-old has compelling 5f form at Good and Firm (10/15 sim-going, 1W7P including two seconds at this trip) and Gina Mangan gives 5lb, making this the central horse around which the entire race revolves.

runners_data.name: River Edge
runners_data.note: Long-absent three-year-old (736 days off, form reading 452/) trained by Christopher Mason alongside Darkened Edge; all three career runs came on Good ground at 5-6f and the form profile is entirely unexposed, giving it a speculative each-way angle if fitness is there.

runners_data.name: Snow Boots
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old carries a fade-in-finish flag backed by sim-going figures of 0W0P in 14 comparable races; 45 days since last run and a history of tracking without landing the blow makes this a difficult proposition in a race where the pace is already predicted to be controlled.

runners_data.name: Titus Thor
runners_data.note: Malcolm Saunders's six-year-old also carries a fade-in-finish flag and figures of 0W0P in six comparable runs; the trainer is 0/1 in the 14-day window and the horse has struggled on Good ground at sprint trips, with its mapped midfield spot masking a true hold-up preference that needs pace it is unlikely to get.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris's three-year-old ran just two days ago — the freshest form in the race — and carries 5lb less than rivals at 130lbs; recent form at 5-6f on Good and Firm has been patchy (two seconds, lots of mid-pack finishes) and its hold-up style requires a faster gallop than this race is likely to produce.

races.paceDynamic: Darkened Edge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Good To Firm sprint at Chepstow and, with no genuine rival to force the pace from the off, Gina Mangan should be able to dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop rather than being dragged into a war. The remainder of the field — Daley T, River Edge, Titus Thor, Bama Lama, Snow Boots and Rogue Rebellion — are all hold-up or midfield types by nature, meaning Darkened Edge faces zero early pressure and can control the fractions entirely. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear, and Banana and Rogue Rebellion are best placed to push forward and apply the nearest semblance of pressure, though neither is a natural front-runner. This race shape strongly favours Darkened Edge and any prominent racer who can track the uncontested leader, as a controlled pace on fast ground at a sharp 5f circuit rewards those who travel sweetly in behind the pace rather than those who need a strong gallop to deliver a late surge.

watchPoints.text: Darkened Edge breaks cleanly — if Gina Mangan gets to the front unchallenged within the first furlong, the race shape is effectively set and no hold-up horse in this field has the form or pace to reel her in on Good To Firm ground over 5f.

Banana's return from 246 days off is the single biggest wildcard; if Scott Dixon has the mare fit, she is the most likely horse to push forward and test Darkened Edge early, fundamentally altering the pace scenario from a solo lead to a genuine duel.

Watch Rogue Rebellion's draw and early stride — having run just two days ago, it is either cherry-ripe or ring-rusty; a horse carrying 5lbs less than rivals could exploit a compressed mid-race scenario if the jockey elects to track the leader rather than drop in.

River Edge's 736-day absence means any signs of greenness or early reluctance from George Wood should be noted immediately; Christopher Mason trains both River Edge and the leader Darkened Edge, so stable tactics could become a factor in how this race is orchestrated.

Snow Boots and Titus Thor both carry official fade-in-finish flags — if either shows atypical early foot and pushes to the front, it may create a brief false pace impression before fading, which could compress the field and inadvertently benefit Darkened Edge coming home.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 8f on Good going with Jason Watson aboard, drawn to lead and dictate; her STYLE_FIT tag signals she is operating slightly out of her most comfortable role as a prominent racer, but with no pace rival to challenge her, she is the dominant shape-setter here.

runners_data.name: Violet Goldsmith
runners_data.note: Callum Hutchinson partner handles Good ground adequately (2/5 on similar going) but the 35-day absence for Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is a consideration; a natural hold-up runner who will need pace to sustain and rivals to tire before she can make inroads in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a major jockey upgrade for George Scott's consistent filly who won over this trip on Standard and placed on Good; a hold-up operator who will need to be produced late, though her recent placed record at 8f suggests she gets the mile well on most surfaces.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans's filly brings strong Good-going form (4/9, 1W4P on similar ground) and the visor adds a behavioural focus; returning quickly on four days' rest, she is the natural prominent tracker and Mason Paetel's 5lb claim preserves her light weight advantage.

runners_data.name: Paean Of Appin
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's runner has a very shallow form pool (three runs) with a fade pattern in finishes; a true hold-up horse by nature, she has been mapped to midfield purely because the rear is saturated — her out-of-role positioning and the trainer's 0/6 in the last 14 days both temper expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Very Demure
runners_data.note: Archie Watson fits the blinkered hold-up type for Harry Vigors (5lb claim) and showed a placing at 8f on Good earlier in the season; like Paean Of Appin, she is a genuine rear-of-field operator shown in midfield on the map because the true hold-up berths are full — her chance depends on a stronger pace than Buckland Belle is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) takes on this unknown-style debutant at the trip; only three runs recorded, all in modest company, with no win or placing — the trainer's 0/9 in 14 days and complete absence of mile form make him a speculative quantity in a race that will test tactical positioning early.

runners_data.name: Anorah Unleashed
runners_data.note: Dr Newland & Insole's filly steps up in trip from 6-7f wearing a hood and tongue-tie combination for the first time; returning off 18 days with four consecutive placed efforts suggesting consistency, but the step to a mile on fast ground is an unproven jump and her unknown style makes positional reading difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Buckland Belle is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she is likely to stride into a comfortable lead from the off and control tempo on Good to Firm ground over Chepstow's flat mile. Alice's Influence is the only other prominent-style runner and will track Buckland Belle, creating a race that develops at a sustainable, measured clip rather than a scorching gallop. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Very Demure and Paean Of Appin are true hold-up horses by nature but have been redistributed to midfield because the rear is congested; in reality, neither is likely to be closer to the pace than their natural style demands, and their out-of-role positioning weakens their chance in a shape that suits them. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader, moderate tempo, strong ground — firmly favours prominent or just-off-the-pace runners who can sit on the leader's shoulder and produce a clean, unobstructed finish rather than horses who depend on a true end-to-end gallop to close into.

watchPoints.text: Buckland Belle has no rivals to challenge her for the lead — watch whether Jason Watson allows her to coast at a falsely slow tempo, which could compress the field and give hold-up horses a winning opportunity they would not otherwise have.

Very Demure and Paean Of Appin are genuine closers who have been mapped to midfield due to field composition — if either ends up further back than their mapped position, their already-slim winning chance shrinks further given the likely moderate tempo.

Alice's Influence runs just four days after her last start and carries 133lbs; watch in the paddock for any sign of fatigue or freshness that might affect Mason Paetel's ability to hold the prime stalking position throughout.

The Good to Firm ground is faster than the card heading of Good suggests — all seven races on the day are being run on Good to Firm, which meaningfully advantages horses with sharp, prominent pace rather than those who rely on grinding stamina.

Ernie McCrew and Anorah Unleashed are both unknown-style runners stepping up in trip; watch their early positioning in the first furlong, as where they slot relative to Buckland Belle will largely determine which scenario they can realistically contribute to.

runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip on good ground, giving Double Naughty genuine course-and-distance credentials; nevertheless a genuine hold-up horse working out of position in a field heavy with backmarkers, so Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) will need fortune in running to replicate that win.|

runners_data.name: Maid In Devon
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly carries the lowest weight in the field and arrives on the back of back-to-back wins in soft and good ground; as a natural come-from-behind type squeezed into midfield by the density of hold-up horses here, she needs clean air to confirm that recent improvement is genuine.|

races.paceDynamic: Moscow Power is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outset, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good To Firm ground at Chepstow's straight six. That controlled tempo — neither dawdling nor searingly fast — classically compresses the field and makes it difficult for closers to generate meaningful momentum from off the pace. The race shape therefore favours prominent racers who can sit just behind Moscow Power, avoid the sprint for cover in the early stages, and pick up efficiently in the final two furlongs. It is worth noting that this field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Evie Ross, Double Naughty, and Maid In Devon are genuine come-from-behind horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning several runners will be competing for ground they do not naturally occupy, likely producing traffic issues for at least one of them. Blue Orbit and Grey Horizon, as natural prominent types, are best placed to capitalise on a single-pacemaker scenario where sitting a length or two off the leader and travelling through the race is the winning move.

watchPoints.text: Moscow Power (J: Jason Watson) — if it fails to break cleanly or gets crowded off its lead, the entire race shape collapses and no scenario plays out as mapped; watch the start closely.

Evie Ross, Double Naughty, and Maid In Devon — three genuine hold-up horses all competing for the same late ground; at least one is likely to get badly hampered or face a wall of rivals two furlongs out, creating a significant non-runner effect for late closers.

Grey Horizon (headgear: visor, 10-day turnaround) — if the visor sparks early keenness and it burns too freely behind Moscow Power, it could compromise its own finish and tighten up the pace picture unexpectedly.

Star Material — 58-day absence and a weak recent form string makes it the most vulnerable to fitness concerns; if it shows early it has trained well this will be notable, but its erratic sectionals could also disrupt the mid-division runners around it.
